title: Payal Kapadia, Anurag Kashyap Joined by Kavita Gupta’s Cineroost as Producer on Prateek Vats’ ‘Chronicles of a Confession’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Kavita Gupta’s U.S.-based Cineroost has boarded Prateek Vats’ second feature, “Chronicles of a Confession,” as producer, joining Payal Kapadia and A
body:
Kavita Gupta’s U.S.-based Cineroost has boarded Prateek Vats’ second feature, “Chronicles of a Confession,” as producer, joining Payal Kapadia and Anurag Kashyap on the project, which starts shooting in early November.

	Cineroost stepped in to handle global representation and U.S. markets, and to help get the film into production. It is the company’s next feature after Vir Das’ “Baara Number.”


	Penned by Vidur Nauriyal, Vats and Shubham, the drama centers on a Kashmiri shawl seller who admits to a crime he didn’t commit, kicking off a series of events nobody saw coming. The script was chosen for the Busan International Film Festival‘s Asian Cinema Fund, under its script development strand.
	

	Vats broke through with “Eeb Allay Ooo!,” which world premiered at the Pingyao Film Festival in 2019 and took the Golden Gateway award at the Mumbai Film Festival that year. The film went on to screen at the Berlinale in 2020 and at Tribeca’s first online edition.


	Ranjan Singh of Flip Films (“Songs of Forgotten Trees,” “Vagachipaani”) produces alongside Dubai’s Action Filmz, India’s Etched Films and Khan & Kumar Productions (“Lovers in the Blue Night”). The project’s producing and creative base stretches across India, the U.S. and the U.A.E. Kashyap and Kapadia serve as executive producers.

	Kashyap, who was involved in Vats’ first film, said the director had spent a long time on a script he envies. “I almost want to steal it. And since I can’t, I have jumped on board as an executive producer,” Kashyap said. “It is an honor to associate with someone as great as Payal Kapadia who I have seen sticking to her voice and her ground as a filmmaker and then there is my own producer Ranjan Singh. What was there in this to not want to be part of it.”
	

	Anand Bansal (“Dhuin,” “Gamak Ghar,” “The Elephant Whisperers”) is behind the camera, with Rajesh Thanickan (“Santosh,” “Homebound”) as supervising producer. Devika Dave (“Boong,” “Sherni”) handles production design, Himani Dehalvi (“Trial by Fire”) costumes and Bigyna Dahal (“The Fable,” “Khauff”) sound design.

	“Prateek’s films mix humor and political commentary in a unique way which I have always admired. And this new project takes this to an even higher level,” Kapadia said.

	“‘Chronicles of a Confession’ has been brewing for some years and I am thrilled that it is going on floor now,” Vats said. “The film solidifies my collaboration with producer Ranjan Singh, who has been with me since my debut feature, ‘Eeb Allay Ooo!'”

	Gupta’s earliest film projects, 13 years ago, were with Kashyap, and the two have remained close. “Strong writing, the best creators and a stellar global creative team, everything about this film aligned with my vision for Cineroost – rare, global and rooted,” Gupta said.

	The film marks the second major step in building out Cineroost’s slate.

	“Business from films is not for my sustenance but really for my soul and passion,” Gupta said. “I find that to be a strength in the work I do in the creative world. I have the privilege of flirting with risk more than others.”

	“A lot of my work for South Asian talent and projects has been under the radar,” she added. “I felt time has come for me to take bigger steps and come out from being in the shadows to do what I love, nurturing creative voices, enabling stories that matter and building bridges between divergent worlds.”

title: ‘Marshals’ Star Luke Grimes Says He Hasn’t Spoken to ‘Yellowstone’ Co-Star Kevin Costner ‘Since We Stopped Working Together’
description: Kevin Costner and Luke Grimes may have played a father-son duo on-screen in “Yellowstone,” but off-screen, the two actors haven’t spoken since Taylo
body:
Kevin Costner and Luke Grimes may have played a father-son duo on-screen in “Yellowstone,” but off-screen, the two actors haven’t spoken since Taylor Sheridan’s Western drama concluded.

	“I’ve never spoken to Kevin since we stopped working together,” Grimes, who now stars in the “Yellowstone” spin-off “Marshals,” said in a recent interview with USA Today. “Not for any other reason other than just, you know, we’re both busy guys and life moves on.”
	

	“Yellowstone” ran for five seasons and came to an end in December, 2024. Costner appeared as the family patriarch, John Dutton, while Grimes played John’s youngest son, Kayce. Grimes appeared on the show throughout the duration of its run, while Costner’s character was killed off and subsequently did not return for the final six episodes of the show that made up Season 5B.


	When asked if Costner would make a future appearance in “Marshals,” the actor said it “would be cool,” though he noted, “I doubt that will happen at this point.” He continued: “I just don’t know… I think, if there was a flashback, I’d probably rather it be with Monica than John. I think that’d be more poignant to the character, but we’ll see.” (Grimes was referring to Monica Long Dutton, Kayce’s wife, played by Kelsey Asbille. Her character has died of cancer by the time “Marshals” premieres.)

	“I think that’d be more poignant to the character,” he said. “There’s been no conversation, but I sure would love it. I love working with her.”

	Per the official “Marshals” logline, the spin-off follows Kayce as he ventures beyond Yellowstone Ranch and joins an “elite unit of U.S. Marshals, combining his skills as a cowboy and Navy SEAL to bring range justice to Montana, where he and his teammates must balance family, duty and the high psychological cost that comes with serving as the last line of defense in the region’s war on violence.”
	

	Season 1 of the show premiered earlier this year in March, while Season 2 premiered Sunday.

title: Charlamagne tha God on Mental Health, Social Media and Prioritizing Real-Life Connection: ‘You Got to Constantly Weed Out Your Garden’
description: Charlamagne tha God has built a prolific career as a radio host, television presenter and mental health advocate. He has co-hosted the nationally sy
body:
Charlamagne tha God has built a prolific career as a radio host, television presenter and mental health advocate. He has co-hosted the nationally syndicated radio show “The Breakfast Club” since 2010, and he and his fellow hosts were inducted into the Radio Hall of Fame in 2020 for their work on the show. 

	Though he has dabbled elsewhere, the radio personality emphasized that “audio is still king” while in conversation with Variety‘s Cynthia Littleton at the Variety Experience and Culture Summit: The IRL Advantage presented by OUTFRONT, during which he also shared how he has created events and shaped his content to support and meet people where they are.
	

	In 2019, Charlamagne founded the Mental Wealth Alliance, a nonprofit organization that hosts an event on Oct. 10, World Mental Health Day, to provide a space for people to hear from mental health professionals for free.

	Charlamagne, who wrote about his anxiety struggles in his 2018 book “Shook One: Anxiety Playing Tricks on Me,” emphasized the importance of access to mental health services, particularly for the Black and brown communities the organization is designed to serve. “It’s a free event because I feel those type of resources and that type of information should be free.” 

	The event is streamed live on YouTube, often on “The Breakfast Club” channel, which has 6.1+ million followers. But when thinking about the event’s resonance, Charlamagne brings it back to reality. “It’s funny we’re talking about IRL like it’s culture, as if we all don’t live real lives every single day,” he said.
	

	Charlamagne is also the founder of the Black Effect Podcast Network, which hosts a yearly festival in Atlanta featuring live podcast tapings. His biggest takeaway from the event, which held its fourth iteration in April, is seeing people show up.

	“We really got to get back to creating a sense of community around all of these things that we’re doing,” Charlamagne said. He described the way people interact with phones and social media as “verbally abusive relationships.” The platforms are useful, he said, but “you got to constantly weed out your garden.”

	With the rise of the creator boom, which yielded success this year for former YouTubers Curry Barker (“Obsession”) and Kane Parsons (“Backrooms”), Charlamagne talked about the ability to capitalize on a platform. “I guarantee you, there’s a creator online right now that none of us in this room know about. They’re probably only getting 100 views per video, but they’re making something amazing,” he said. “Don’t wait until that person gets 10 million followers or 10 million views to pay them attention.”

	Charlamagne said the connection he has found through terrestrial radio is the foundation of what he does: “Every morning I know that I’m a person’s habit.” “The Breakfast Club” has hosted interviews with modern political figures, including Kamala Harris, Zohran Mamdani and former presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. 

	Looking toward the midterm elections this November, Charlamagne said, “I think it’s going to be a lot of people that show up to the voters’ booth thinking about those high prices of gas, thinking about the cost of groceries, and realizing that they’ve been lied to.”

title: ‘Star Wars: Galactic Racer’ Debuts on Amazon Luna Day and Date With Wide Release (Gaming News Roundup)
description: “Star Wars: Galactic Racer” launched on Amazon’s gaming service Luna day and date alongside the game’s worldwide release across platforms including
body:
“Star Wars: Galactic Racer” launched on Amazon’s gaming service Luna day and date alongside the game’s worldwide release across platforms including PlayStation 5, Xbox Series S and X and PC.

	Developed by Fuse Games, the studio behind the “Burnout” and “Need for Speed” franchises, “Star Wars: Galactic Racer” puts players behind the controls of a range of repulsorcraft in a racing circuit in a galaxy far, far away.


	Set early during the New Republic era, the game introduces the Galactic League, an unsanctioned racing circuit assembled by Darius Pax. Players step into the role of Shade, a lone racer dreaming of glory and revenge. The high-stakes racing takes place across “Star Wars” planets like Jakku, the Graveyard of Giants, Ando Prime or Sentinel I.
	

	“We’ve always believed Luna players deserve to be in the action from day one, and Star Wars: Galactic Racer makes that a reality for the first time,” said Jeff Gattis, head of gaming at Amazon. “Luna players can jump into the single-player campaign today without needing to own a console or wait for a lengthy download. And the best part: if they’re a Prime member, they already have it at no additional cost. It’s exactly the kind of experience we want to deliver on Luna, and we think players are going to love it.”

	Prime members can start their engines on Amazon Luna on the same day as other platforms and play the single-player campaign.

	See more gaming news from the week in the roundup below.
	
		PARTNERSHIPS/COLLABS	

	Zara Larsson is collaborating with Winx Club for a limited-edition card from trading card brand Kayou.
	

	Dressed in her outfit from the “Midnight Sun” music video, the card features Larsson posing alongside the Winx Club fairies. The collaboration will debut at New York Comic Con, which begins Thursday and goes until Sunday.

	Kayou will also offer cards featuring “KPop Demon Hunters,” “My Little Pony” and “Monster Jam” at this year’s comic con.

	*

	Discord is teaming up with The Living Tombstone on an original Halloween track and a Halloween remix of the Discord ringtone.

	The Living Tombstone’s new original track, “Don’t Hang Up the Call” and accompanying video are inspired by the quirks of how people actually spend time together on “Discord.” The Living Tombstone is putting its own spin on Discord’s iconic ringtone for the season.

	The Living Tombstone’s have turned gaming and internet fandom into music inspired by the games and culture their fans love. Over 30 million users take part in personal, gaming and interest-based servers each month, including 7.2 million in music communities.
	
		NEWLY ANNOUNCED GAMES	

	During RuneFest 2026 over the weekend, developer Jagex announced new content coming to “RuneScape,” “Old School RuneScape” and “RuneScape: Dragonwilds,” as well as an upcoming fourth “RuneScape” MMO game.

	Still early in development, the as-yet-unnamed title will “bring the world of Gielinor to life in Unreal Engine, combining the depth, freedom and community-led spirit that have defined RuneScape for 25 years with the technology and game design possibilities of today,” per the team.

	“RuneScape Reignited” launches Dec. 2, inviting players old and new to return together and rediscover “RuneScape” with the ultimate RuneScape experience.

	Players can get full Reignited Access without a membership from Dec. 2 to Dec. 12. The Plugin API is launching in October, with players getting an early hands-on ahead of official release.

	“Hoard of Dragons” kicks off in January, offering a sequel to the popular “Dragon Slayer” quest, “City of Gnomes” continues the gnome storyline, first stated in 2002 and “Secrets of Karamja” introduces a new end game raid. These arcs weave together “RuneScape”’s 2027 content into three distinct story narratives and also include an agility skill rework, new skilling and solo bosses, new area expansions and a new “Grandmaster Quest.”
	

	“Luminance,” a brand-new update serving as a prelude to 2027’s “Blood Crystal Saga,” launches in December this year, and features the introduction of the Elves into “RuneScape: Dragonwilds,” new elven-themed customisation options for player characters and buildings alike and the Prayer skill. “The Blood Crystal Saga” kicks off in 2027 starting with the Song of Rebellion in early 2027. Official modding arrives on “Dragonwilds” in 2027 through a new partnership with CurseForge.

	*

	Step into the castle! “The Traitors” fans can now test their scheming skills with “The Traitors: Interactive Game” on iOS and Android platforms, Fusebox Games announced on Monday.

	Players begin by choosing a defining trait: the outspoken leader, the adaptable chameleon or the chaotic wildcard, which will form the foundation of your character.

	Set across 12 days, 22 players emulate the TV show at the castle by building trust with other players during missions as well as building believable theories during The Round Table.

	“When it comes to adapting iconic entertainment IP, Fusebox Games is as faithful a partner as they come,” Fusebox Games CEO Terry Lee said. “Our history is built on story-based, choice-driven games that put players in control, making the deceit and strategy of The Traitors a natural fit. We’re giving fans the chance to step out of the audience and take a seat at the table and tell their own story at the castle.”
	
		TECH	

	Google is introducing “Playground,” an experimental gaming platform that lets users create, play and share fully custom games with no coding experience required. 

	With “Playground”’s conversational interface, users can create custom games by typing what they want, remixing starter prompts or getting guided support to help them share their creativity with the world. Users can refine the rules with prompts, customize characters and tweak the environment until it’s what they envision. “Playground” is browser-based, games are playable across phones and laptops.

	Once a game is ready, users have the option to keep their game private, generate a shareable link to send to friends and family or publish it to share with the broader “Playground” community. Since “Playground” supports multiplayer gameplay, gamers can also see in-game leaderboards and follow other creators to see their latest creations.
	

	The upcoming “Unity Spark Integration: Playground” will soon offer integration with UnitySpark so creators who want to expand their concepts can take advantage of Unity Spark’s robust, professional-level mechanics, 3-D capabilities and the flexibility of the Unity runtime.

title: Sundance-Winning Producer Neeraj Churi Boards Awedacious Originals’ Busan Title ‘About an Intimate Matter’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Sundance-winning producer Neeraj Churi has boarded “About an Intimate Matter” (Ekanto Byaktigoto Bishoy), a Bengali-language queer drama from Awedac
body:
Sundance-winning producer Neeraj Churi has boarded “About an Intimate Matter” (Ekanto Byaktigoto Bishoy), a Bengali-language queer drama from Awedacious Originals that will world premiere at the 31st Busan International Film Festival.

	Churi, of Lotus Visual Productions, produced Rohan Parashuram Kanawade’s “Sabar Bonda” (Cactus Pears), winner of the World Cinema Grand Jury Prize: Dramatic at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival. 


	“About an Intimate Matter,” a psychological drama about a schoolteacher whose private photographs are leaked by a student, is the first Bengali-language production for Awedacious Originals. Written and directed by first-time feature filmmaker Sandeep Kumar Paul, the film is in the festival’s A Window on Asian Cinema section. Sreya Bhattacharya, Shimlli Basu and Sanjita Das lead the cast.
	

	The story centers on Swarna, a high school science teacher, and her partner Driti, who relocate to a quiet suburban town to start over. Their plans fall apart when one of Swarna’s students finds intimate images of her online and passes them around his class. The gossip hardens into something more official, as fellow teachers and school authorities start to treat her personal life as a disciplinary matter. With her job and her relationship both under strain, Swarna has to decide how far she will go to take back control of her own life.

	“Having ‘About an Intimate Matter’ start its festival journey at Busan is deeply meaningful to me,” Paul said. “The film grew from years of listening, observing and trying to understand how profession, class and social expectation enter our most private relationships. I did not want to look at queer lives from the outside or treat them as exceptional. I wanted Swarna and Driti to have the same contradictions, desires, vulnerabilities and dignity as anyone else.”
	

	The project has its roots in Paul’s photography. In 2016 and 2017 he shot Pride walks and other gatherings in Kolkata, but came to feel that still images couldn’t carry the emotional weight of the lives he was documenting. A close friend’s struggle to square his identity with the expectations of those around him made the story more personal. Paul wrote the screenplay in close collaboration with queer friends, whose experiences shaped the characters and dialogue.

	The film’s look tracks Swarna’s state of mind. In its early stretches, Paul deliberately keeps the sky out of the frame, letting it creep back in as she finds her footing. He shot in the 1.66:1 aspect ratio to press in on her, and set the story in winter, when bodies stay covered and movement is restricted.

	Apoorva Bakshi, the International Emmy-winning producer of “Delhi Crime” who co-founded Awedacious Originals with Monisha Thyagarajan, said the company had been drawn to Paul’s voice and the understated way he handles identity, intimacy and social prejudice. “There is a remarkable restraint to the film; it never announces its politics, but allows them to emerge through its characters, their relationships and the world they inhabit,” Bakshi said. “We’re incredibly proud that ‘About an Intimate Matter,’ our first Bengali-language production, will begin its journey at Busan, and we could not imagine a more meaningful home for its world premiere.”

	Bakshi and Thyagarajan produce alongside Churi and Abid Aziz Merchant of Lotus Visual Productions, with producing partners spread across India, the U.K. and the U.S. Jenisha Dave is associate producer. Churi, a queer cisgender man, also contributed his perspective during development and production.

	“Swarna’s circumstances are specific, but the desire to live and love without being made answerable to public judgment is universal,” Churi said. “Busan gives us the opportunity to carry her story beyond its geographical setting and into a larger international conversation.”

	Raised in Kolkata, Paul trained in engineering and business before starting out in Bengali theater, later moving into illustration and street and documentary photography. 

	Awedacious Originals, which has offices in California and India, produced documentary series “The Hunt for Veerappan” for Netflix and documentary feature “Womb” for Prime Video, as well as hand-drawn animated feature “The Glassworker,” which premiered at Annecy in 2024. The company’s festival slate also includes “Madina,” a co-production with Kazakhstan that premiered in Tokyo, and short “Aman,” a trans pregnancy drama that was a finalist in the Short Cuts competition at Toronto this year and is set for its European premiere at the BFI London Film Festival.

title: ‘Carrie’ Star Samantha Sloyan on Modernizing an Iconic Evil Mom, Playing a Character Who ‘Chooses Violence’ and Being Mike Flanagan’s Secret Weapon
description:
“Why would I do ‘Carrie’ now?”

	Samantha Sloyan says this was one of the first things writer, director and showrunner Mike Flanagan said to her whe
body:
“Why would I do ‘Carrie’ now?”

	Samantha Sloyan says this was one of the first things writer, director and showrunner Mike Flanagan said to her when he revealed his idea to turn Stephen King’s 1974 novel of the same name into a miniseries. 

	Sure, Flanagan had tackled King before, adapting novels such as “Gerald’s Game” and “Doctor Sleep” into acclaimed feature films. But “Carrie” had already been adapted into one of the most famous horror movies of all time, a 1976 masterpiece by Brian De Palma which contained many indelible, nightmarish images. 
	

	Additionally, Flanagan was interested in recruiting Sloyan to play Carrie’s religious and antagonistic mother, Margaret White, unforgettably played by Piper Laurie in the film.


	But, much like Carrie on prom night, Flanagan wanted to burn it all down.

	“He just took everything down to its studs, and then rebuilt the structure,” Sloyan says. 

	What’s left is a modern tale of school bullying, with a Margaret who is both a zealot and also, thanks to Sloyan, much more human than in the past.

	Sloyan is in the enviable position as a loyal member of Flanagan’s stable of actors, and she’s a scene stealer in many of his darkest projects. From their first collaboration in the 2016 movie “Hush” to roles in series like “The Haunting of Hill House” and “The Fall of the House of Usher,” she’s chameleonic in her parts. But perhaps most memorable to horror fans is Sloyan’s lead role as the villainous yet piteous Bev Keane in “Midnight Mass,” in which she weaponized her religious values and became more terrifying than the vampires roaming the seaside town.
	

	Sloyan often hears about these projects in their earliest days, given a personal connection: She’s been best friends with Kate Siegel, Flanagan’s wife and frequent collaborator, since their twenties.

	“We’ll be having dinner and cleaning up and he’ll kind of saddle up and just be like, ‘What do you think about Carrie?’ Something like that,” she says. “I’m always like, ‘I don’t … what do you mean?’”

	Given her striking work as Bev, it’s easy enough to draw a straight line to Margaret, who in the original text is much more outrageous in her faith. But Sloyan sees two truly different and complicated characters.

	“What Mike did with ‘Carrie’ is so much of the horror element: we’re following people along this path and seeing all these times where they could have chosen to behave this way, but instead chose to behave this way,” Sloyan says. “Bev’s on a path for her own glory in a way that’s very single-minded, that’s very selfish, that’s very manipulative. But Margaret is protecting the daughter that she loves. In doing that, Mike sets up all these times as they’re interacting with this world that’s totally new to Carrie and that Margaret has purposefully removed herself from for 15 years. And there’s all these opportunities where she can choose to learn or engage or participate. Instead, she just always chooses violence, to push back, to try to destroy, to undermine, to manipulate.”

	Sloyan’s childhood was diametrically opposite to Carrie’s existence, in that she was born to two character actors who encouraged her to become engaged with the world.

	“I was born into it, and being raised by character actors, you’re surrounded by really fantastic stories and all different types of people,” she says. “You might recognize them on the screen, but these aren’t people who are walking through life with celebrity having warped everything. But the lifestyle looked so scary because it was so unpredictable and insecure in so many ways.”



	

					Samantha Sloyan as Bev Keane in “Midnight Mass.”
									EIKE SCHROTER/NETFLIX
	



	Sloyan followed in their footsteps, racking up an impressive roster of recurring roles on hit shows like “Scandal,” “Grey’s Anatomy” and even the first season of “The Pitt” (she plays the grieving mother whose son overdoses on Fentanyl).
	

	But she’s always excited to hear about roles for Flanagan’s projects, because they often push her beyond her own expectations.

	“One of the cool things about Bev when Mike said, “I’m hearing you for this,” there was nothing I had done for him that would have indicated that was a character I could do,” she says. “That was really exciting. As an actress, a character like that was thrilling and terrifying. But the second I read her, I understood how she talked, how she moved, what her deal was. With these characters, Margaret and Bev, the connector is obviously Mike Flanagan, who has written people good, bad and complicated. He is writing people we recognize.”

	That depth and confidence allowed Sloyan to look past previous depictions of Margaret.

	“What I was worried about as an actress was trying to thread was how Margaret was so tangibly dangerous, and that I really wanted Carrie to be stuck,” she says. “You need her to be stuck between these kids in school and her home and not have anywhere to go. So I could love Carrie, but I couldn’t be loving in the way she needed. So I had to make sure that Margaret — and it’s written that way, but also just in my portrayal — could cut Carrie off from her and her love when Carrie wasn’t doing what Margaret needed her to do. That threat of removal of the love.”

	Despite that dark undercurrent, stories like “Carrie” are the ones that keep Sloyan energized as an actor.

	“I’m still blown away by something that I’ve never seen or been a part of before,” she says. “That’s exciting. There’s a lot to be said for the amount of content that’s being made, but it does mean there are a lot more things to be a part of, that’s for sure.”

title: Miles Teller to Be Honored by Newport Beach Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Miles Teller will be honored with the Artist of Distinction Award at the Newport Beach Film Festival.

	He will be presented with the recognition at
body:
Miles Teller will be honored with the Artist of Distinction Award at the Newport Beach Film Festival.

	He will be presented with the recognition at the fest’s annual Honors ceremony on Oct. 18.

	“Miles Teller brings extraordinary dedication to every role he takes on,” Newport Beach Film Festival CEO and executive director Gregg Schwenk said. “He consistently delivers standout performances in both major blockbusters and character-driven indies, and we are thrilled to celebrate his career in Newport Beach.”
	

	Teller next stars in James Gray’s thriller “Paper Tiger” alongside Adam Driver and Scarlett Johansson. The film follows two brothers who become entangled in a dangerous criminal underworld. The film will screen at the Newport Beach Film Festival on Oct. 18. Neon will release the film in theaters on Nov. 13. 


	Teller’s credits include his performance as Bradley “Rooster” Bradshaw in Paramount’s “Top Gun: Maverick,” his breakout role in Damien Chazelle’s “Whiplash,” and his portrayal of producer Al Ruddy in the limited series “The Offer”. Teller’s other recent work includes A24’s “Eternity,” Apple TV+’s “The Gorge,” and dramas such as “The Spectacular Now,” “Only the Brave,” and “Bleed for This”. He is currently in production on the crime thriller “Copperhead.”

	Teller joins previously announced Newport Beach Film Festival honorees KJ Apa, Sosie Bacon, Gemma Chan, Jonás Cuarón, Sarah Finn, Mckenna Grace, Justin Hartley, Taraji P. Henson and Jack O’Connell. 

	The festival takes place on Oct.15-22. In addition to “Paper Tiger,” this year’s program also features screenings of “A Talent for Murder,” “Behemoth!,” “Ink,” “Josephine,” “La Bola Negra,” “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York” and “Wild Horse Nine.”

title: London Film Festival Hails the ‘Great Andrew Scott’ as ‘Elsinore’ Opens 70th Edition With Tears, Cheers and ‘The Ethel Merman Disco Album’
description: The 70th BFI London Film Festival kicked off on Wednesday with the European premiere of “Elsinore,” a movie that, as the credits rolled, left large
body:
The 70th BFI London Film Festival kicked off on Wednesday with the European premiere of “Elsinore,” a movie that, as the credits rolled, left large swathes of the audience at the Royal Festival Hall wiping away tears. But just moments later, as the name of lead star Andrew Scott appeared on stage, the loud snuffles were replaced with whoops and, in rather uncharacteristically British style, a standing ovation for the actor.

	Directed by Simon Stone from a script by Simon Beresford, “Elsinore” — already expected to be among the awards season hopefuls — sees Scott portray famed Scottish actor and “Chariots of Fire” star Ian Charleson. In 1989, while already succumbing to complications from AIDS, Charleson replaced Daniel Day-Lewis in “Hamlet” at London’s National Theatre after the actor had walked off stage mid-performance, never to return to the production. Charleson received rave reviews, but died just seven weeks after bowing out.
	

	Speaking on stage ahead of the premiere, Stone introduced his cast, including “the great Andrew Scott.” While Scott said little before “Elsinore” began, afterwards he made a special presentation in which he called up the real-life individuals from the film and the actors portraying then, including the National Theatre’s stage doorkeeper for 46 years, Linda Tolhurst (played by Monica Dolan), itss long-serving dresser Ralph Mills (Paul Chahidi), and director and Charleson’s close friend Sean Mathias (Matthew Beard). But the biggest round of applause — and other standing ovation — was reserved for pioneering HIV/AIDS consultant Dr. Margaret Johnson (Olivia Colman).
	

	“It’s difficult to underestimate the impact this person had on the development of treatment for people suffering with HIV and AIDS,” said Scott. “To our mind, she is a true life hero.”

	Scott then signed off by introducing a song from camp classic “The Ethel Merman Disco Album,” performed in the film, as a tribute to Charleson. “We want you to be able to remember not just Ian’s death, but how extraordinarily he lived with such flair and zest and warmth and charm and passion and talent,” he said, adding that the song “encapsulates this man who loved this industry so much.” 

	Encouraging the audience to dance as they left the auditorium, Scott concluded: “He went out performing, so this one’s for you, Ian. We love you.”

	Speaking to Variety before the premiere, LFF head Kristy Matheson said she’d first seen “Elsinore” — which has amassed widespread critical acclaim since premiering in Telluride — with colleagues during the summer. “It was one of those films where we walked out and we just had to really take a beat,” she said. “We were really so sure of the film from the second it finished.”

	Bringing “Elsinore” to London as the curtain raiser not only felt like a perfect choice for the festival, but offered some considerable poignancy given the location of the opening night premiere — merely meters from where Charleson gave his final performance.

	“I think it’s going to be such an incredible moment to screen that film literally a stone’s throw away from the National Theatre,” said Matheson. “So it feels like we’re going to bring this film home, and I’m just really excited and honored to do that.”

	The London Film Festival runs Oct 7-18, with other major screenings including the likes of “Wild Horse Nine,” “La Bola Negra,” “Club Kid,” “Ink,” “Artificial,” “Primetime” and “The Debut” and a lineup of Screen Talks involving the likes of Danny Boyle, Cynthia Erivo, Sofia Coppola, Javier Bardem and John Malkovich.

title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Star and EP Brendan Hunt on the Season 4 Finale’s Surprise Job Changes, and Whether There Will Be a Season 5
description:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for the Season 4 finale of “Ted Lasso,” now streaming on Apple TV.

	There’s a new coach at AFC Richmo
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for the Season 4 finale of “Ted Lasso,” now streaming on Apple TV.

	There’s a new coach at AFC Richmond, and it’s not Ted Lasso. The Season 4 finale of “Ted Lasso,” titled “The Departing Lass,” ended with Ted (Jason Sudeikis) handing the AFC Richmond women’s team manager job to Alice Chilton (Tanya Reynolds), while he demotes himself to assistant manager alongside Coach Beard (Brendan Hunt).
	

	Alice is ready for the challenge, having been instrumental in the team’s rise. And at the same time, it turns out Ted has been thinking about his father lately — who died by suicide when Ted was just 16 — and realizing that he still has been absent too much for his own son Henry, he knows it’s time for a change.


	Meanwhile, there’s also a switchup on the men’s team, as Roy (Brett Goldstein) has been offered — and has accepted — a huge job managing the Chelsea team. But he and Keeley (Juno Temple) are about to have a child, so he has a lot to ponder. Not to be outdone, Rebecca (Hannah Waddingham) proposes marriage to her boyfriend Matthijs (Matteo van der Grijn).

	And as the team mourns the death of pub owner Mae (Annette Badland), she winds up saving the day from beyond the grave. That’s because Zelda (Tracey Ullman) is ultimately thwarted in her attempt to buy up a controlling interest in AFC Richmond by Mae’s last will and testament, which gives her shares in the team back to Rebecca — keeping her at 51% ownership.

	Oh, and Nate (Nick Mohammad) drops by to visit Nelson Road — and take part in a reunion of the Diamond Dogs, who are called into duty when Roy asks for advice on being a new dad. And Beard, having gone through some midlife crisis looks this season, gets a haircut.
	

	That’s a lot of story, not to mention a new version of the opening theme, now performed by Brandi Carlile. 

	Hunt, who also serves as an executive producer and writer on “Ted Lasso,” spoke with Variety about the Season 4 finale — including whether there will be a Season 5.
	
		Let’s start by talking about how the season ended. There was a little bit of a fake-out when Roy was leaving, so it seemed like Ted was going to ask Rebecca for that job again. But instead, he was going to ask her about demoting himself. How did that come about?	

	That was something Jason wanted to happen from the beginning of the writers’ room. He saw Ted stepping down as just kind of fundamental to what the season was going to be. Which is why Episode 1 starts with the close-up of his nametag to “Lasso assistant manager,” and then we land on Ted Lasso as an assistant manager at the end. In terms of the fake-out, yeah, just a tiny little goose for the last moment. For anyone who still thought somehow this was like a side dalliance with the women’s team — “ha, I knew he’d come back” — no, we’re not. We’re quite fond of our women’s team, thank you very much!
	
		We see Ted still feels like he’s not spent enough time with Henry, and that lays the groundwork for him deciding to pull back. What was the discussion in the writers’ room of what Ted’s journey would be this season?	

	The Henry thing is the main thing. The whole idea of bringing Henry to London this time, he thought in his head, “now I’ll have much more time with Henry” — and it hadn’t worked out that way. He’s missed his games, and especially as he’s reminded by the Employee of the Year plaque that his record-setting father bequeathed him unwittingly. You can be a little too devoted to your work, and it can be deleterious to to your health. He just wants to make sure he’s with Henry more. And then, as a side channel to that, he’s watched Alice grow. She was almost ready when we first met her, and now she’s much more ready. I think he is just ready to be support personnel at this time, and have more of his free time, and see what he can do with it.
	
		Was there ever a thought of letting Zelda actually take over AFC Richmond, perhaps as a cliffhanger for next season?	

	We definitely thought about every option for that, including, “OK, what would it be if there’s a new boss here that everyone has to deal with, and what would happen?” But in the end, we said, no. This is this is Rebecca’s roost, and she’ll figure this out.
	
	
		Speaking of cliffhangers, there aren’t too many this season. But there are still some threads to pick up on. What did you want to leave hanging to address in Season 5?	

	There’s not much in the way of cliffhangers. But Ted and Beard as peers instead of hierarchically, I’m curious about that. Roy and Keeley becoming parents, curious about that. Rebecca married, curious about that. The fellas running the pub, and how’s the team going to take to Alice as their leader? These are all just more like questions than cliffhangers. But also, there’s not yet any indication that we’re going to get to answer those questions. So at the moment, they’re still lingering in the air.
	
		That brings up the key question. What what do you hear about a Season 5? What does Jason want to do in terms of coming back?	

	He plays the cards close to his chest, and I’m not privy to whatever poker game that I hope is happening between the powers that be. I think we’ve always basically hoped we were coming back for more than one, but if it ends up just being one, then OK, that’s fine. It did end nicely. We’ll just have to see.
	
		We actually saw more of Mae this season, which made what happened at the end of Episode 9 even more impactful. Did Mae have to die for Rebecca to save the team?	

	We had the notion of, if we are going to lose Mae, then the phrase that kept coming up was, how can Mae save the team from the grave? And so we got ourselves toward that. Shout out to to Annette Badland, who is just so beloved by all of us, and such a trooper. Once Jason told her what was happening, she rolled with it.
	
		But tell me about the decision process of having Mae pass away.	

	It’s one of the landmarks of life that we go through, and we haven’t exactly gone through it on the show, at least with someone who we know or care about. Like, we never knew Rebecca’s dad, for example, but we were at his funeral. But Mae seemed like the right person for it to be, and then dealing with all the repercussions of it. And then, how can she, in death, just basically save the day.
	
		All right, let’s talk about Beard. He starts wearing color contacts, he changes his hair and starts wearing earrings. How was it decided that he was going to be put through the wringer this season? 	

	Especially by the end of Season 3, we know that yes, Beard has a fairly sturdy facade, but he’s basically always had demons. We learned that really when we went on Beard’s after hours as well. As someone who also has always dealt with his own self-image issues, it’s like you can, in his case, get to the Ted effect. You can like get to as good a place as you can get. But you still have stuff that you’re dealing with, and you need to be dealing with it. And essentially, the Jane situation of being without Ted for so long has just rattled him. That’s left him in a vulnerable position. The point of all that being like, there’s only so much other people can do for you. You have to get yourself to the healthiest place. And he’s just not able to for a while here, in the aftermath of the Jane stuff. And then when he thinks he’s gonna rise up from that on New Year’s, there’s another gut punch that he takes there. All that is a long-winded way of saying, it’s just a good old-fashioned midlife crisis — but with modern cosmetic choices.
	
	
		And Richard Schiff apparently plays a version of Beard in Jane’s play!	

	I love Richard Schiff, and I hope he gets a kick out of that, because I know he watches the show. So that was a very intentional choice to shout out to the legend.
	
		How do you know he watches the show?	

	We just literally crossed paths at the Emmys one year. The year that I presented with Jane Lynch — and we didn’t even get to talk much. That was the year they were doing all the reunions of old casts, and at one point just crossing to my seat, here comes the whole cast of “The West Wing.” Richard Schiff in particular, was just beaming at me in this warm and wonderful way. It was very clear, like “Oh wow, Richard Schiff digs the show. That’s really great.” So this is our shout out.

	
		For this final episode, you managed to get back some of the other familiar faces from the series, like Nick Mohammed. Were there any folks that you weren’t able to get, or you hoped to get, that you wanted to for Season 4?	

	There was no one who negotiated themselves out of it or anything. Anyone we thought of to go to, we went to. We were letting the story decide largely. Should we come back, we haven’t gotten everyone, and there’s still at least a few people who we would want to say hi to at some point. 

	I’m still a little surprised that we didn’t get any Sassy time. Everybody loves Sassy, and we love Ellie Taylor so much as well. But everyone who we thought of and could rationalize story-wise was kind enough to come hang out.


	
		You had a runner this season of Ted’s chair constantly being too low. You knew you had to pay that off, and you did. Where did this running joke come from?	

	Every once in a while, Jason’s got an idea in his head that he doesn’t take the time to explain for whatever reason. Not out of malice or anything, he just doesn’t. We’ve got plenty of other things to talk about on set. But somewhere around episode three or four, he was like, “I think my chair is gonna be broken.” OK, great. And then the next episode, “I think my chair is gonna be broken again.” Oh, fine. And then a month later, “It’s been Alice — it’s been Alice the whole time.” That’s great! 

	So yeah, this is one of those things where he sees the whole map and he’s just gonna walk you down it. He doesn’t necessarily need to tell you everything that’s coming up. We don’t need to know everything. We’ll find out eventually. But yeah, I was pretty tickled. As I hope everyone else will when they find out that was the reason.
	
		We’ll call it Chekhov’s chair.	

	Yes, if you will.

	This interview has been edited and condensed.
